strategy.summary: Motorenwerk Saalach is a sound, group-owned motor maker (sup:70580) and the sole active source for part:350013 (IE4 30 kW, 100% quota, framework ctr:4600070580). It is only a qualified, uncompetitive bidder on part:350011, where Nordmark holds the business. It is deprioritising us as a small, 'not strategic' account (news:20260327-07, doc:20260908-70580-M3, doc:20260926-70580-M1). Its delivery and quality have become excellent (sc:70580@2026Q3). Its main grievance is our chronic late payment (doc:20260612-70580-P). Copper is sharply up, so increase requests on 350013 are plausible and checkable. The price on 350013 sits only slightly above our should-cost (cost:350013), so there is little room to cut. Our strengths are: rising volume shared with them (fc:350013@2026-09), a qualified alternative source (Nordmark), the annual price-notice and renewal clauses, and its habit of settling well below its ask. The strategy is to hold or limit increases by trading what it values (on-time or faster payment, binding and growing volume, a 24-month commitment, possibly a copper clause), not by squeezing margin.
strategy.decision_maker: Key account manager handles routine moves; price changes above the 2% threshold go to the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks (doc:20260322-70580-M2). A new sales director sets account priorities and currently sees us as non-strategic (doc:20260926-70580-M1).

findings.text: Part 350013 (IE4 30 kW, sole source at 100% quota): current price EUR 1608.32 sits only +2.6% above our should-cost of EUR 1567.90 (its own plant, no margin, error about 5%). The margin is thin, roughly within the estimate's error. There is little room for a cut on cost grounds, and a hard push risks leaving a stabilise-type supplier below a healthy margin.

Part 350011 (IE3 7.5 kW): Saalach quoted EUR 421.06 on 2026-09-03, +12.3% over the should-cost of EUR 374.95. That estimate is of Nordmark's plant (sup:70510), not Saalach's, so it is a weaker benchmark. Nordmark supplies at EUR 348.32 (2026 price) and quoted EUR 381.47 in 2024. Saalach is uncompetitive here: about 17% above our current price and above should-cost even before margin.

Cost drivers favour the supplier. Copper is +47.7% over 12 months and at its 36-month peak; with a weight of about 0.19-0.20 this means about +9% on price. Steel is +6.5% (about +1.1%) and labour +2.7% (about +0.6%). The weighted total is roughly +11% since autumn 2025, while the 2026 renewal gave only +1.7% (350013). A cost-based increase request is therefore plausible and checkable.

Counterpoints for us are weak:
- Steel is -6.3% below its 36-month peak and -26.7% below its 2022 high, but neither figure is checkable.
- Power prices are -43% against 2022, but power is not a listed driver.
The copper peak argues for an index clause rather than a fixed increase, so we avoid locking in a peak price.

Price history for 350013 has been flat: 1606.06 (2023), 1581.52 (2024-25), 1608.32 (2026), +0.1% since 2023. The supplier historically settles about 3 percentage points below its ask; it asked +3.3% and got +1.7% at the 2025 renewal. The 2026-09 quote is list price, stock only, with 7-day validity, a sign of reduced interest.

Overall room on price: on 350013 essentially none downward. A realistic target is to hold EUR 1608.32 or limit any increase to the copper share via an index clause. On 350011, Saalach's quote is well above Nordmark's price; there is no reason to award it unless it drops toward about EUR 375-385.

findings.text: Decision ladder: price changes above 2% need their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Any counter above 2% costs at least one committee cycle. Offers within 2% can be closed by the key account manager.

We are being deprioritised. They are refocusing on large key accounts and new product lines, and small customers are to be moved to standard ranges. A new sales director called our volumes 'not strategic', and replies have been slower since summer. Our spend of about 0.6% of their turnover confirms we are small to them.

Our late payment is their main grievance and our biggest weakness. 97.1% of invoices are paid late, on average 19.3 days after due and up to 40 days. They warned in writing on 2026-06-12 that they would review conditions. Paying on time or faster is a cheap trade they visibly value.

They are financially sound and cannot be pressured by distress. Group owned, 182 M EUR turnover, 30.2% equity ratio, stable credit index 171, VDA 6.3 grade A. They can afford to walk away from a small account.
Their performance has become excellent: 95.8% on time and 0 ppm. They will cite this as a reason to deserve recognition. Acknowledging it costs us nothing.
Their style is formal and process-driven, with fixed deadlines such as call-offs for January due by 10 December (plant closed 23 Dec to 6 Jan).
Leverage for us: rising forecast volumes and a lower-priced second source. The contract can still be stopped by notice by 2026-10-02.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070580 covers only part:350013 (IE4 30 kW). Prices are fixed per calendar year, and any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2026-10-02 for 2027. Without timely notice the 2026 price of EUR 1608.32 carries over.

The term ends 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless either side terminates with 90 days' notice, so the deadline is 2026-10-02. Both sides can exit, and the supplier, which calls our volume 'not strategic', could use it too. As of the data date (2026-09) a few days remain to act.

Payment is 30 days net, against our 60-day standard, and delivery is DAP with a 42-day lead time. Quality terms are a 95% OTD target and a flat EUR 150 per complaint, which is low. We pay late: 19.3 days on average, 97% of invoices late. The supplier formally complained in 2026-06 and threatened to review its conditions. This is a contract breach on our side and weakens our standing.

Renewal history on part:350013: asked +2.4% and settled -1.5% (2023); asked +3.9%, settled 0% (2024); asked +3.3%, settled +1.7% (2025). Settlements average about 3 pp below the ask. The gap is shrinking, so the supplier is getting firmer. The price is roughly flat since 2023 (1606 to 1608).

Dependency is asymmetric. Saalach holds 100% of part:350013. Nordmark (sup:70510) is qualified with 0% quota and quoted -7% in rfq:6000000123 (2024), so a credible second source exists. On part:350011 Saalach is only qualified at 0%; Nordmark holds 100%, and rfq:6000000202 is open. Our spend of about EUR 1.15M is 0.6% of Saalach's EUR 182M turnover. Tooling is n/a in the sourcing records, although the argument library claims the supplier owns it; this is inconsistent.

findings.text: Delivery has improved steadily: rolling OTD rose from 60% (2024Q3) to 95.8% (2026Q3), score 80 to 97.9, amber B to green A. The last 12 months had 24 receipts and only one was late, by 28 days. That single miss is the only lever on delivery, and it is weak.

Quality is clean. There is 0 ppm and no QN for the last 21 months. The only QN (qn:20004373, leakage at test, Dec 2024, 1 pc) was closed with an 8D in about 30 days and EUR 150 was recharged. Peers' median is 457 ppm. This record argues its case, not ours.

Our volume outlook for part:350013 is rising. The 2026-09 forecast is 964 pcs for the next 12 months against 720 ordered in the last 12 months (+34%), and it has been shared with the supplier. Received qty is stable at about 720-740 per year. This is our main counter to its stated 'small account' stance.
Price for part:350013 has crept up: 1606.06 (2023), 1581.52 (2024-25), 1608.32 since 2026-01. That is +0.1% against the first orders while performance improved. Should-cost is 1567.90 (+2.6% gap).

part:350011 is not supplied by this supplier in the order data; it is bought from sup:70510. Its forecasts and orders only matter as a bundling or rival reference. Evidence of 350011 business with Saalach is thin.

Deliveries data has a known issue: requested and confirmed dates differ by 10-30 points (KNOWN_ISSUES 1). One recent PO was confirmed 4 days later than requested (po:4500014388-10). Delivery figures beyond the scorecard should not be over-argued.

arguments.text: Copper is our largest volatile input and has risen about 48 % in a year to a 36-month peak. On an IE4 30 kW motor (190 kg, copper-heavy windings) that alone justifies an increase well above the 1.7 % we accepted for 2026.

Our price is already at cost. Your own bottom-up estimate puts our cost at EUR 1,567.90 with no margin, against EUR 1,608.32 today. That is about 2.5 % gross over cost, before copper moved. There is nothing left to squeeze.
Steel is up 6.5-7.3 % and labour 2.7 %. Together with copper, that covers more than half of our cost base, all moving up.
Our delivery and quality are now excellent: 100 % on time in 2026Q2 and 95.8 % over the last 12 months, 0 ppm since 2025, class A. That performance costs money and has value to you.
You pay late on 97 % of invoices, on average 19 days over terms. That is unpaid financing we carry, and it is part of our cost to serve you.
We have shown restraint for years: -1.5 %, 0 % and +1.7 % against our asks of 2.4 %, 3.9 % and 3.3 %. We have absorbed rises before, and we cannot this time.

weak_points: Nordmark is qualified on 350013 and quoted EUR 1,495.59 in 2024, about 10 % below us (quote:7100049).
Our 350011 quote of EUR 421.06 is far above Nordmark's EUR 348.32 and above should-cost, which undermines our credibility on pricing.
Power prices are down 43 % versus 2022, and iron castings are up only 1.8 %.
Steel is still 26.7 % below its 2022 high.
The 2027 price change needed written notice 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2 October. If we missed it, the price rolls over.
Our 7-day list-terms quote and the 'not strategic' remarks look like we are pushing them away. They may decide to move to Nordmark.
Our history of settling far below our asks invites them to discount whatever we ask.
Our lead-time record was poor before 2025 (60-71 % on time).
The should-cost estimate has only 5 % confidence, so they can dispute it either way.
wants: Payment on time at 30 days, or faster. This is worth a meaningful price discount to us.
Binding annual volume of at least 900-960 pcs, in line with their forecast.
A copper index clause in place of a full fixed-price increase. With that, we could accept a low base increase.
Bundling: an award of part of the 350011 volume, which would raise the account to key-account size.
Call-offs placed before our holiday shutdown.
red_lines: No price below about EUR 1,600 fixed without a copper clause or payment fix, since that would mean selling at or below cost.
Any increase above 2 % needs our pricing committee, so we cannot agree to it on the spot.
No penalty or chargeback higher than the current EUR 150 per complaint without a price offset.
No continuation of late payment without consequences.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the strong year together: 0 ppm and close to 100 % on-time delivery. Copper is up 48 % in twelve months, and steel and labour are rising too, while your own cost estimate shows our margin on 350013 is under 3 %. We therefore propose +4.5 % from 1 January 2027 at fixed price. Alternatively, we can offer +1.9 % with a copper index clause, a 24-month term and binding volume of 950 pcs. Either way, we expect payment strictly on 30 days, because overdue invoices remain a serious concern for us.

rebuttals.answer: We agree that copper has risen sharply and we do not dispute it. Put in proportion, our category estimate gives copper roughly a fifth of the motor's cost, so the rise supports a share of the price, not the whole of it. Some of that cost is already in the current price, which was set for the calendar year under the framework. Copper is volatile in both directions, so building today's peak into a fixed price would lock in the top of the cycle. We are open to a copper-linked clause with a fair base, or a fixed step sized to the copper share, paid for with terms you value.

We accept that the margin on this motor is thin, and we are not seeking a cut. The estimate itself carries a sizeable error band. It therefore supports holding the price steady with a fair adjustment, not a large increase. Our aim is a healthy supplier, and we would rather fund that through volume, commitment and payment than through a higher unit price alone.

The steel and labour rises are real, but they are moderate. Weighted by their shares of cost, each adds only a small fraction to the price. Taken together with copper, these drivers support a measured adjustment rather than one well above last year's. We will look at the combined effect with you on that weighted basis.

Your delivery and quality turnaround is genuinely excellent and we thank you for it; it is one reason we want to deepen the relationship. That same performance meets the targets already set in our quality agreement. We see it as the basis for a longer, larger commitment from us rather than as a separate price element.

You are right, our payment discipline has not been acceptable, and we apologise. We will commit to paying on contractual terms. We are also willing to discuss faster payment as part of the package, which removes that financing cost from your side at its source. It is better fixed directly than recovered through the unit price.

We appreciate the restraint you have shown in past rounds, and the last renewal already brought an increase. Even so, over the whole period the price has not fallen, so the relationship has been fair to both sides. With volume now growing, we would like to find a balanced outcome together again.

press: Could you confirm whether written notice of a price change for next year was sent within the period set by our framework agreement, so that we work from the same basis?
Our forecast for this motor, which we share with you, shows clearly rising volume, and we would like to understand which commitment would bring us into your key-account service level.
Would a combined package covering both motor types, at a price on the smaller motor closer to current market levels, change how you view our account?
We would value an offer sized so that your key account team can agree it without waiting for a committee cycle.
We would welcome firmer validity and supply terms than list conditions from stock, since we intend a longer partnership on this motor.
